tools.name: create_grid
tools.description:
POST /: create a grid, your own store of items; no API key needed. Returns its `api_key`, shown only now:
pass it as `api_key` to every other tool, or send it as the header `Authorization: Bearer hg-…`. It holds up
to `max_items` items, queries included. Each address may create only a few grids a da

tools.name: get_grid
tools.description:
GET /: the grid the API key opens: its name and its limit on items, `max_items` (queries included; null:
no limit).

tools.name: delete_grid
tools.description: DELETE /: delete the grid and everything in it, items, queries and grades; its key stops working.

tools.name: put_item
tools.description:
PUT /items/key: write the item at `key` (e.g. "42", no leading /), creating it or replacing its content.
Text is a string and a record a JSON object, each up to 8 KB; an image its bytes as base64, kept as a WebP of
at most 512 px (its width and height come back); an emb a list of floats from the gri

tools.name: get_item
tools.description: GET /items/key: the item at `key`, with its `content` as put_item takes it.

tools.name: delete_item
tools.description: DELETE /items/key: delete the item at `key`, and every grade of it.

tools.name: list_items
tools.description:
GET /items?prefix=: `items`, those whose keys start with `prefix` (e.g. "tools/"; all by default), in key
order, without their content (get_item reads one), at most `limit` (1 to 100, 32 by default). `next`: for the
next page, pass it as `after` (null: this was the last).

tools.name: create_query
tools.description:
POST /queries: store a question to ask of the items, its content as put_item takes it. Returns its `id`,
which the other query tools take. Its results are ready at once; ask again with the same `id` rather than
creating the same query twice, so its grades add up.

tools.name: get_query
tools.description: GET /queries/id: the query `id`, with its `content` as create_query takes it.

tools.name: delete_query
tools.description: DELETE /queries/id: delete the query `id` and its grades.

tools.name: get_results
tools.description:
GET /queries/id/results: `results`, the query's best items under any of `prefixes` (e.g. ["tools/"]; all
items by default), best first, each with its `score`, DNA's estimate of the grade you would give it (on the
grades' scale once the grid has some; before, only the order means anything), as list_i

tools.name: put_grade
tools.description:
PUT /queries/id/grades/key: grade the item at `key` (as get_results returns it, e.g. "42") for the query `id`.
`score` is from -1 (wrong) to 1 (right), anything between for partly right; it trains DNA and replaces the
grade before. Grade the results you judged, typically the first few.

tools.name: get_grade
tools.description: GET /queries/id/grades/key: the query's grade of the item at `key`.

tools.name: delete_grade
tools.description: DELETE /queries/id/grades/key: forget the query's grade of the item at `key`.

tools.name: list_grades
tools.description: GET /queries/id/grades: `grades`, the query's grades, {"key", "score"}, in path order.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_grid" references sensitive artifacts (api_key, authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "put_item" is 755 chars, far longer than this server's median (97). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.
